newsitem.title: USA: Venezuela stocks seen doubling by end of 1997.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela stocks seen doubling by end of 1997.

text.p: The Venezuelan stock market index should nearly double by the end of next year, Bear Stearns & Co analyst Geoffrey Dennis said on Tuesday.
"We think there will be a very big turnaround," he told Reuters.
Dennis said the continued rally from the market's low point in October 1995 would be fueled by:
-- an economic rebound arising from stabilization of the bolivar currency and inflation falling to 25 percent next year from about 100 percent in 1996;
-- a rise in world oil prices, which benefits oil-producer Venezuela;
-- payoff of government debt from windfall oil revenues;
-- and privatization, including sale of the government's 40 percent stake in CANTV, the state telecommunications company.
"Our existing end-1996 target for the ICB (stock market) index is 7,500, up from just over 6,000...at present," he and analyst Julie Dykstra wrote in a recent report.

"We introduce here an end-1997 target for the ICB of 14,000, or in dollar-adjusted terms, 24.55, a gain of 93 percent from current levels. Therefore we expect the Venezuelan equity market to virtually double again over the next 12 months."
Among Venezuelan stocks, Dennis and Dykstra have assigned a buy rating to Ceramica Carabobo, a construction materials company.
They rated foods company Mavesa S.A. attractive and cement company Vencemos S.A. neutral.
